main_text.l: Theologiae in Illustri, quae Lugd. Batav.
tenebris Tartareâ se fulse meri, strepitusque nefandos.

l.i: Ætherea ne damnare minus, prob numina gentem.
Sic se Erebi ostens aut acies, sauceque dolique
Et quicquid nex dira parit. Vesana libido
Heu! demissis grassatur agris, nec meta furori est.
Quis mihi Cajanos, Alogos, Bassosque; Secundosque
Nota) Dietrepbi, Garthaeis, ac fata Menandri?
Quis mihi vel fando memoret Barbasq;, Naetosque,
Impatiens mens horret adhuc. Si Tartara plaudant
Ut vis est vesana illis, si vincere cordi est
Et Domini calcare acies longo ordine, gyris
Inflexis, nec scire modum; Tu surgis in hostes
Impavidus, vir magne, truces, & vindice coelo
Sicque alios, Te ipse beas. Nihil arma Pelagi
Mentibus officiunt cautis, nihil arma Socini

page.notes: The initial woodcut letter "A" is decorative; the first word "Aeternus" is joined to it. Several words in the italic verse are damaged and uncertain (e.g. "sauceque", "Dietrepbi", "Naetosque", "Barbasq;"), and the scan is blurred; these readings are best effort.
